triage.method: title/abstract relevance pass over every verified official record, followed by full-text review of the strongest load-bearing candidates

papers.load_bearing: A unified 18-class weight-only coupling map scales to 1.3e11 candidate channels and produces cross-model causal induction interventions.
Controller-class equivalence, population-target equivalence, causal nonidentification, and a strict interventional regret separation form a coherent theorem chain.

papers.reason: Strong sparse-latent theory and PushT evidence, but the practical claim remains benchmark- and predictor-capacity-dependent.
Elegant quotient theory, but synchronized simulator branches, finite actions, short horizons, and controlled state environments limit the current empirical claim.
Invariant correction is specific and falsifiable, but tested on one pendulum with three seeds and modest nonuniform rollout gains.
Rigorous nonequilibrium second-law extension, but validation is confined to analytically/numerically simple driven double-well examples.
Rich phase phenomenology and kinetic theory, but several phase boundaries are approximate and finite-time/finer-grid sensitivity remains open.
Promising high-dissipation estimator, but current evidence is simulation-based and the learned variational estimator lacks broad independent stress tests.
The Chern-parity theorem is novel, but reentrant behavior is demonstrated on one minimal five-state network with very small late-time gaps.
